passage: When the ordering system in the Lisbon office went dark at ten past two, the chat filled with people typing at once. Beatriz wrote, 'I'll be incident commander. Olga, you investigate. Mateus, you talk to customers and management.' Then she asked everyone else to stay quiet in the main thread unless called on. Olga opened the logs and posted findings every ten minutes. Mateus sent a short note to the support desk and another to the director, and promised the next one at three. Beatriz kept a running list of what had been tried. Nobody dug through the same log twice, and nobody talked over anyone. At ten to four the fix went in and the system came back. Beatriz thanked each role by name and set a review for the next morning.

qa.q: Who did Beatriz tell to investigate?
What did Beatriz want when she asked everyone else to stay quiet in the main thread?
qa.a: Beatriz wanted calm and focus, so that the investigator and the person sending updates could work without being talked over.

qa.q: What could the team add if an outage ran for many hours?
qa.a: The team could rotate the roles after some hours so people stay rested, using the running list to hand over.

qa.q: How might the director have felt about Mateus's updates?
qa.a: The director would probably feel informed and calmer, since the notes came when promised.

grounding: Shows a team naming one incident commander, one investigator and one person who updates customers and management.
